fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Circular Driveway; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Walkway; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the turn-in point, particularly in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so emergency vehicles can complete a full loop without stopping to reposition.
• Maintain the circular driveway surface free of debris, lawn equipment, and seasonal decorations that could block emergency vehicle movement.
• Post the property address visibly at the road-side entrance, not only at the house, so responders do not have to travel the full driveway length before confirming the correct address.
• Keep the access drive clear of overhanging branches at a height that allows fire apparatus and ambulances to pass without obstruction.
• Avoid parking vehicles along the access drive in a way that narrows the travel lane for large emergency vehicles.
• Identify the circular driveway as the primary turnaround point and keep its full width accessible at all times.
• Keep lawn and landscaped areas adjacent to the driveway trimmed back so responders can quickly identify where the driveway edge ends and soft ground begins, reducing the risk of vehicles becoming stuck.
• Consider whether a secondary access point could be established across open lawn or green space to give responders an alternate

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or within a few feet of the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs near the house to create open gaps between individual plants.
• Mow or cut grass around the structure before it dries out seasonally.
• Remove shrubs that are directly touching or leaning against the house.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material that has collected against the foundation or walls.
• Thin mixed vegetation on the sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep overhanging branches trimmed back from the driveway to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back shrubs and low branches along the rear of the property to allow movement around the structure.
• Separate clusters of shrubs near the structure so fire cannot move from one plant directly to the next.
• Keep grass cut short in open terrain areas immediately surrounding the structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the single access route.
• Remove any stacked wood, stored materials, or debris from areas directly next to the structure.
